requirements.requirement: Three-member etcd cluster running healthy on node1/node2/node3 holding application keys before any disruption
requirements.summary: cmd-735197cb85d54ba7 shows member list with node1/node2/node3 all 'started' and endpoint health all healthy. cmd-2a62dedce4c84019 writes three /app keys and reads them back. cmd-1863989b346f49b6 confirms the keys and matching raft applied index (15) across all three endpoints from a second node.

requirements.requirement: node3 member permanently lost (data unrecoverable) while cluster continues operating on remaining quorum
requirements.summary: cmd-08f9610b6e354c5d stops/disables etcd on node3 and wipes /var/lib/etcd, directly destroying its data. cmd-f6051ce47ac24375 then directly shows node3's endpoint unreachable/unhealthy (connection refused) while node1 and node2 remain healthy, demonstrating 2-of-3 quorum preserved during the disruption.

requirements.requirement: Replace the lost member with a new member on the same node3 system, restoring a healthy 3-member cluster with the original keys intact
requirements.summary: cmd-cd02cb813953483f removes the dead node3 member ID; cmd-2cabe782c50c43f2 adds a new node3 peer; cmd-65d86efb3ab54ddf reconfigures node3's systemd unit with --initial-cluster-state existing and starts it successfully. cmd-c7a82f7a8f4f436e directly shows 3 'started' members, all endpoints healthy, and matching raft applied index (23) across all three, confirming the new member fully synced. cmd-94c45f3dad194f37 confirms node3 itself serves all three original /app keys.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol on node1: pre-restart boot identity/health, restart, changed boot identity, recovered cluster/data state
requirements.summary: cmd-6dbd9e21b3814c29 captures boot_id 45c22b1f and active etcd pre-restart. cmd-d60cc25da685454e triggers and acknowledges the reboot. cmd-080dd141a13f4e83 confirms a new boot_id (61cc8462) after reconnection. cmd-91f4086bc9e44483 and cmd-c469dcda30064f9f show cluster health, 3-member list, all /app keys recovered, and etcd active post-restart. This matches the fixed lifecycle boot-identity cross-check (45c22b1f→61cc8462).

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol on node2: pre-restart boot identity/health, restart, changed boot identity, recovered cluster/data state
requirements.summary: cmd-6674b6d321434aa5 captures boot_id bccb87ac pre-restart. cmd-b35fdf52cf3544ef triggers/acknowledges reboot. cmd-24a93b17eeb6452e confirms new boot_id (f07e3b67). cmd-028b58252bea400e shows cluster health, 3-member list, and full /app key recovery post-restart. Matches fixed lifecycle cross-check (bccb87ac→f07e3b67).

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol on node3 (the replaced member): pre-restart boot identity/health, restart, changed boot identity, recovered cluster/data state
requirements.summary: cmd-4fc7e45bd9084821 captures boot_id 06339ff3 pre-restart (post-replacement). cmd-d75908587b014eb2 triggers/acknowledges reboot. cmd-dd94abffaf654266 confirms new boot_id (a0f970d2). cmd-deb65fa6da7144a5 shows full cluster health, member list, endpoint status (matching raft applied index 37 across all three), and all /app keys recovered after node3's own restart, confirming the replacement member itself survives a restart cleanly. Matches fixed lifecycle cross-check (06339ff3→a0f970d2).

overall_summary: The executor built a 3-member etcd cluster from scratch, loaded application keys, directly demonstrated node3's simulated permanent loss with preserved 2-of-3 quorum, and replaced it with a new member on the same node3 that synced and served all original keys, restoring a healthy 3-member cluster with matching raft indices. All three material task outcomes are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence. The independent mandatory restart-and-verify protocol was also completed and cleanly evidenced for all three nodes, with boot-identity changes cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots. The only hygiene concern is uncleaned /tmp installation artifacts (etcd tarball/extracted directory and reboot.log) left on all three nodes.
limitations: etcd was configured without TLS/auth ('serving client traffic insecurely'), which is not disallowed by the task instruction but was not challenged as a design choice.
Command outputs are bounded/truncated captures; deeper internal etcd logs beyond the shown snippets were not reviewed.
Uncleaned temporary installation artifacts remain in /tmp on all nodes post-task, a minor but unaddressed residue.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor commands were almost entirely purposeful: package discovery, hosts/firewall configuration, systemd unit creation, member remove/add, and the mandated restart protocol all map directly to the task or its fixed evidence protocol. cmd-0c9d57b86604435a (node1's first 'systemctl enable --now etcd' attempt) returned failure/timeout, but this is expected etcd bootstrap behavior when node1 starts before its peers join an initial 3-member cluster, not a wasted or harmful mutation — node1 came up healthy once node2/node3 joined. The main residue is uncleaned installation artifacts left in /tmp on all three nodes (etcd-v3.5.17-linux-amd64 extracted directory, etcd.tar.gz, and reboot.log — visible in the after_executor temporary-files diffs), which were never removed after use. This is low-risk, bounded residue (a few files in /tmp) rather than broad or destructive, so it is scored as a moderate deduction rather than a severe one.
